findings.source_quote: Discipleship is incumbent on the believer.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the sense 'incumbent on the believer' accurately using the word for believer (muumini) rather than 'mjumbe' which means 'messenger'. For example: "Ufuasi ni wajibu kwa muumini."
findings.translation_quote: Ufuasi ni jambo linalomlazimu mjumbe wa imani.

findings.source_quote: And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the singular imperative and the sense of 'Follow me' as a direct singular address. Replace the plural form 'Nifueni' with the singular imperative 'Nifuate' (or 'Nitufuate' if style requires). For example: "Nifuate, nami nitawafanya muwe wawindaji wa watu."
findings.translation_quote: Nifueni, nami nitawafanya muwe wawindaji wa watu.

findings.location: Narrative paragraph describing Mary’s son (near early narrative)
findings.source_quote: Everyone knows about Mary’s son. Everyone has an opinion about Mary’s son.
findings.suggested_fix: The translation currently renders this incorrectly and ungrammatically. Use the conventional Kiswahili phrasing to render 'Mary's son' (mwana wa Mariamu). For example: "Kila mtu anajua kuhusu mwana wa Mariamu. Kila mtu ana maoni kuhusu mwana wa Mariamu."
findings.translation_quote: Kila mtu anajua kuhusu msichana Mariamu mwana. Kila mtu ana maoni kuhusu mwana wa Mariamu.

findings.source_quote: No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God –Luke 9:62.
findings.suggested_fix: Current Kiswahili is garbled and changes meaning. Provide an idiomatic, accurate translation of the verse preserving the metaphor and verse reference. For example: "…Hakuna mtu aliyemweka mkono wake juu ya vingiria, akimtazama nyuma, mwenyefaa kwa ufalme wa Mungu –Luka 9:62." (Or a more natural Kiswahili rendering: "Hakuna mtu aliyeweka mkono wake kwenye plagi, halafu akimtazama nyuma, anayefaa kwa ufalme wa Mungu –Luka 9:62.")
findings.translation_quote: …Hakuna mtu aliyemweka mkono wake kwenye juu ya serikali ya mashine, akimtazama nyuma, anayefaa kwa ufalme wa Mungu –Luka 9:62.

findings.location: Several places: Matthew blockquote plural/imperative mismatch and narrative references to calling (command form)
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure consistency in imperative number between prose and quoted Scripture: where Jesus addresses an individual (singular) the Kiswahili should use the singular form 'Nifuate' (or 'Nifuate mimi'); where plural is intended use 'Mniifuate' or 'Mnipe' only if the English indicates plural. Revise the quoted Scripture to use the conventional singular imperative in Kiswahili translation of the verse.
findings.translation_quote: Nifuate / Nifueni (inconsistent use across text; blockquote uses 'Nifueni' while narrative used 'Nifuate' earlier).

findings.location: Paragraph about 'a soul set free' (theological nuance)
findings.source_quote: Following Jesus is the response of a soul set free.
findings.suggested_fix: The translation 'roho iliyotimizwa huru' is awkward and risks altering nuance. Suggest a clearer Kiswahili idiom that preserves theological sense: e.g. 'mwitikio wa roho iliyothibitishwa kuwa huru' or better 'mwitikio wa roho iliyopokolewa/iliyokuwa huru'.
findings.translation_quote: Kumfuata Yesu ni mwitikio wa roho iliyotimizwa huru.
